transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining me. As you know, we're reviewing the proposed eighth-grade makerspace program before I make a final authorization decision. The draft calls for 24 students supervised by one STEM teacher, using soldering stations, hand tools, a laser cutter, standard metal components, and cloud-based CAD files, meeting twice a week during the spring semester. Following our usual practice, I'd like to hear from each of you on the implementation aspects relevant to your roles. Could we start with you, STEM teacher — what can you tell me about supervising this program?

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to flag some important safety findings. I completed a room-safety review this week, and it found that the makerspace may enroll no more than 16 students. Additionally, any session using soldering stations with more than 12 students requires two supervising adults. The draft program form still shows the original numbers — 24 students with one STEM teacher supervising — so those will need to be revised before this program can be safely authorized.

transcript.text: Thank you all for these critical findings. Let me summarize what needs to be addressed before I can authorize this program. First, from Ms. Rivera: the enrollment must be capped at 16 students, not 24, and any session using soldering stations with more than 12 students requires two supervising adults. Second, from Nurse Brooks: one student has a severe nickel allergy, so nickel-free components are required for that student's participation, and Nurse Brooks must approve the materials list before each session. The health-record review also needs to be documented in the program file. Third, from Mr. Chen: cloud storage is not permitted for student design files. We need an offline design workstation with encrypted USB transfer and an IT malware scan, and the draft program must be updated accordingly. Based on these findings, I plan to set the enrollment cap at 16, require two supervising adults for any soldering session exceeding 12 students, require nickel-free components with Nurse Brooks' pre-session materials approval, and require the offline workstation workflow.
